skill.name: set-up-lightspeed-google-ads-poas-bidding
skill.description: Set up profit or revenue bidding in Google Ads for a Lightspeed eCom (C-Series) store using Product Metrics. Check conversion tracking, review cost inputs, and choose an initial bidding target before making changes in Google Ads.
skill.summary: Guide a Lightspeed eCom campaign from revenue bidding to profit bidding in Google Ads.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most flags are benign documentation or expected integration checks, but the unpinned installer can execute third-party code. The workflow also creates risks around credential handling, unverified browser handoffs, and data sharing beyond profit bidding. No evidence of prompt injection or intentional credential theft was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The workflow allows the assistant to receive a privileged Lightspeed key and secret and pass them to a command.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to enter credentials in the verified Product Metrics app. Remove the agent-side exception and document how to rotate exposed keys.

remediation.issue: The install example does not pin the executable package or the source revision.
remediation.suggestion: Document a verified installer version and an immutable skill revision. Keep installation user-initiated and separate from setup.

remediation.issue: Browser handoffs trust response URLs without a documented destination check.
remediation.suggestion: Check HTTPS and the exact approved provider origin before relaying a link. Reject unexpected destinations and offer official app navigation.

remediation.issue: Profit setup enables additional customer and lifetime value signals through the full conversion set.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the extra signals and obtain explicit approval before enabling them. Offer a profit-only configuration where supported.

content.user_title: Set Up Profit Bidding for Lightspeed in Google Ads
content.value_statement: A Google Ads campaign can meet its revenue target and still lose money after costs. Use Lightspeed order profit to guide Google Ads bidding and choose an initial target.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status and identify unfinished Lightspeed and Google Ads tracking steps.
Guide consent configuration, conversion action setup, and review of product costs, payment fees, and other costs.
Check whether a paid test order arrived and whether it has a profit value.
Suggest an initial target ROAS from current campaign POAS when the campaign report is available.
Give the user steps to change the primary purchase action and verify its status afterward.
limitations: The workflow requires Lightspeed eCom (C-Series), Product Metrics Pro, a proxied Cloudflare domain, and Google Ads with linked Merchant Center.
The user handles store sign-ins, browser approvals, and changes to the Google Ads bidding goal.
Orders with unresolved costs send revenue only. Orders calculated at a loss send a profit value of zero.
New customer, returning customer, and lifetime value bidding are outside this skill's scope.

use_cases.title: Check readiness for profit bidding
use_cases.description: Find out whether your store, consent banner, and Google Ads tracking are ready before changing how a campaign bids.

use_cases.title: Pilot a profit target
use_cases.description: Choose one campaign and use its current profit on ad spend to propose an initial target ROAS.

use_cases.title: Diagnose missing profit values
use_cases.description: Check whether a paid test order arrived with revenue only. Review product costs, payment fees, and cost fallback settings.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Revenue and Profit Bidding
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: learn what changes before reviewing your setup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how profit bidding differs from revenue bidding for my Lightspeed store. Show what a 150% target means when the conversion value is profit.

prompt_templates.title: Review Tracking Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my Product Metrics setup for Lightspeed and Google Ads. List missing steps and tell me which ones I must complete. Do not change settings.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Paid Test Order
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: investigate a missing profit conversion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my paid test order arrived with revenue and profit values. If profit is missing, tell me which consent and cost settings to review.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Single-Campaign Pilot
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a change from revenue to profit bidding.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my selected campaign's current POAS to suggest an initial target ROAS. Show how I can switch the primary purchase action and verify it afterward.

output_examples.input: My paid test order arrived with revenue but no profit. What should I check?
output: The order shows revenue only. Check whether its product costs and additional costs are complete.
In Profit tracking, open Edit costs. Review the product cost fallback and the fixed and percentage payment fees.

output_examples.input: My test campaign has a POAS of 1.5. What target should I start with?
output: Start at 150% target ROAS when the campaign uses Product Metrics - Profit as its primary purchase action.
Test one campaign first. Review its results after a few weeks before adjusting the target.

best_practices: Enter Lightspeed API credentials only in the verified Product Metrics app.
Review consent settings, confirm cost inputs, and verify a paid test order before changing a campaign goal.
Start with one campaign and keep only the intended purchase action primary for that campaign.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse a revenue-based target when switching a campaign to profit values.
Do not make both revenue and profit purchase actions primary for the same campaign.
Do not assume a missing profit conversion means the order broke even.

faq.question: What does POAS mean?
faq.answer: POAS means profit on ad spend. It compares the profit value of attributed orders with advertising spend.

faq.question: Can I keep bidding on revenue?
faq.answer: Yes. Use Product Metrics - Revenue as the primary purchase action for the relevant goal instead of Product Metrics - Profit.

faq.question: Does the assistant change my Google Ads bidding goal?
faq.answer: No. You change the goal in Google Ads. The assistant can explain the steps and verify the conversion action status afterward.

faq.question: What happens if a product cost is missing?
faq.answer: Product Metrics checks the matching Merchant Center SKU cost, then the configured fallback percentage. If neither supplies the cost, the order sends revenue only.

faq.question: Which consent does the profit conversion need?
faq.answer: The documented setup requires both analytics consent and ad user data consent for the profit conversion.

faq.question: What happens when I refund an order?
faq.answer: Product Metrics adjusts the Google Ads conversion after Lightspeed reports the refund.
